claims.evidence: Remote inspection cannot confirm the item's origin or import history.
The witness identified the model name on the camera body in photos 0 and 2.
The witness report does not confirm the condition of the lens glass or the sensor, which determines sharpness.
The witness report explicitly identifies the brand as Canon based on the body and strap markings.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the camera sensor with the lens removed.
risks.if_unproven: as a damaged sensor requiring professional cleaning or replacement

risks.risk: Lens glass fungus or deep scratches
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the front and rear lens elements under bright light.
risks.if_unproven: as a lens with significant optical defects

risks.risk: High shutter count (near end of life)
risks.proof: A screenshot from a shutter count utility showing the total actuations.
risks.if_unproven: as a camera at the end of its mechanical lifespan

risks.risk: LCD screen malfunction or dead pixels
risks.proof: A photo of the LCD screen powered on and displaying the camera menu.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-functional or broken display

proof_requests: Photo of the camera sensor with the lens removed.
Close-up photos of the front and rear lens glass.
Photo of the LCD screen powered on.
Photo of the battery and charger.
response.reason: The seller's claim that the brand is Sony directly contradicts the witness report of a Canon camera. Furthermore, the presence of multiple different camera models (600D and 700D) in the same photo is a common indicator of a fraudulent listing using shop or stock photos.
